Coding Interview Review — FAANG SDE2 / SDE3 / Staff (Java)

Pattern-first review for coding rounds only. Every entry below ends in a tested, paste-ready Java template; pick the topic, read the decision tree, copy the template, adapt the state.

Template-first rule: nothing is listed here without a Java template behind it. The page is generated from the same files that the test suite compiles and runs, so what you copy is what passed the tests.
LeetCode coverage: 2,194 problems map to a template here: 520 named in the template code or practice map, 1,674 matched by a specific LeetCode tag. Each template view lists its problems under the code. Type a problem number or title in the filter box to find its template, or open the LeetCode Coverage view for the full list.

Decision Tree — “which pattern do I reach for?”

Graphs

  1. Unweighted, shortest path? → BFS (multi-source if multiple starts; 0-1 BFS if weights are 0/1)Traversal#bfs
  2. Weighted, non-negative, single source? → DijkstraShortestPath#dijkstra
  3. Weighted, negative edges possible, single source? → Bellman-Ford (also detects negative cycles)ShortestPath#bellmanFord
  4. All-pairs shortest path, dense graph? → Floyd-WarshallShortestPath#floydWarshall
  5. All-pairs shortest path, sparse graph? → Johnson'sShortestPath#johnsons
  6. DAG + need ordering/dependency resolution? → Topological sort (Kahn's or DFS)TopoSortDAG#kahnsTopoSort
  7. DAG + need longest/shortest/count paths? → DP over topo orderTopoSortDAG#longestPathDAG
  8. Undirected + dynamic connectivity/merge queries? → DSUDSU#countComponents
  9. Connect all nodes, minimize total edge weight? → Kruskal's (sparse/edge-list) or Prim's (dense/adjacency-matrix)MST#kruskalsMST
  10. Directed graph, need tightly-coupled clusters? → Tarjan's/Kosaraju's (SCC), condense to DAG if there's a follow-upSCC_Bridges_2SAT#tarjanSCC
  11. Need critical/fragile points in a network? → Bridges & articulation pointsSCC_Bridges_2SAT#findBridgesAndArticulation
  12. Need to traverse every edge exactly once? → Hierholzer's (Eulerian path/circuit)EulerianPath#hierholzer
  13. Boolean 2-variable clause satisfaction? → 2-SAT via implication graph + SCCSCC_Bridges_2SAT#solve2SAT
  14. Assignment/matching with capacity constraints? → Max flow (Edmonds-Karp/Dinic's) or bipartite matching (Hopcroft-Karp)NetworkFlow#edmondsKarp
  15. Small N (≤20), must visit all nodes/subsets? → Bitmask DP (Held-Karp style)BipartiteAndBitmaskDP#heldKarpTSP
  16. Grid, board or string-transformation problem? → Implicit graph: name the node, generate neighbors, BFS (bidirectional if both ends are known)ImplicitGraphs#wordLadder
  17. Shortest path with an extra constraint (K stops, fuel, keys, obstacle budget)? → Put the resource in the state: Dijkstra/BFS over (node, used), or Bellman-Ford capped at K+1 roundsDijkstraVariants#cheapestFlightsDijkstraState
  18. Path cost is the worst edge, not the sum? → Dijkstra with max() as the combiner (or sort edges + DSU)DijkstraVariants#minimumEffortPath
  19. Count the shortest paths, or print one? → Dijkstra with ways[] or prev[]DijkstraVariants#countShortestPaths
  20. Directed cycle, safe nodes, or an order inferred from data (Alien Dictionary)? → 3-color DFS or Kahn's, after building the edges from the dataCycleAndCourseGraphs#alienOrder
  21. Ratios or equivalences between named things (evaluate division)? → Weighted DSU, or DFS multiplying along the pathDSUExtended#calcEquation
  22. Tree question: LCA, distance, diameter, an answer for every root? → Binary lifting, double BFS, or rerootingTreeGraphs#treeDiameter
  23. Small bipartite matching to code live? → Kuhn's; Hopcroft-Karp only for large inputsMatchingColoringFunctional#kuhnMatching
  24. Every node has exactly one outgoing edge? → Functional graph: Floyd's or a timestamp walkMatchingColoringFunctional#cycleStart
  25. Small k-coloring, or "can this be split into k groups"? → Backtracking coloring (k = 2 is the bipartite check)MatchingColoringFunctional#kColorable

Dynamic Programming

  1. Count ways / min cost where step i reads a few earlier steps? → 1D dp, then shrink to O(1) spaceDPLinear#climbStairsO1
  2. Pick or skip adjacent items? → Take / skip state machineDPLinear#rob
  3. Best contiguous subarray? → Kadane (track max AND min if products)DPLinear#maxSubArray
  4. Buy / sell with limits, cooldown or fee? → Stock state machine (hold / sold / rest)DPLinear#maxProfitK
  5. Choose a subset under a capacity, each item once? → 0/1 knapsack, capacity loop DOWNWARDDPKnapsack#knapsack01
  6. Items reusable, fewest items? → Unbounded dp, capacity loop upwardDPKnapsack#coinChangeMin
  7. Count combinations vs ordered sequences? → Coins OUTER = combinations, amount OUTER = sequencesDPKnapsack#coinChangeWays
  8. Can the array be split into equal halves / signs assigned to hit a target? → Subset-sum reductionDPKnapsack#findTargetSumWays
  9. Longest increasing chain? → Tails array with binary search, O(n log n)DPSequences#lengthOfLIS
  10. Two strings, edits or common parts? → Prefix table dp[i][j]DPSequences#minDistance
  11. Does a pattern with wildcards match? → Prefix table; star means skip or consumeDPSequences#isMatchRegex
  12. Can the string be segmented into dictionary words? → dp over prefix lengthDPSequences#wordBreak
  13. Grid with right/down moves? → Row-rolling dpDPGridInterval#minPathSum
  14. Answer for range [i, j] from splitting at k? → Interval dp, loop by lengthDPGridInterval#maxCoins
  15. n ≤ 20, each item used once? → Bitmask dp over subsetsDPBitmaskDigit#minCostAssignment
  16. Count numbers up to N with a digit property? → Digit dp with tight flagDPBitmaskDigit#countDigitOne
  17. dp transition looks at a sliding window of earlier values? → Monotonic deque on dpDPCombined#maxResult
  18. Intervals with weights, pick a compatible set? → Sort by end, binary-search the last compatible jobDPCombined#jobScheduling
  19. Interval DP where equal items attach to a group? → dp[l][r][k] with k attached on the leftDPVariants#removeBoxes
  20. Merge k adjacent piles into one? → dp[i][j][piles]DPVariants#mergeStones
  21. Two walkers on one grid? → Step index + both rowsDPVariants#cherryPickup
  22. Two groups must end up equal? → dp over the differenceDPVariants#tallestBillboard
  23. Eggs and floors? → Flip: floors covered with m movesDPVariants#superEggDrop
  24. Return the actual supersequence, not just its length? → LCS table, walk back mergingDPVariants#shortestCommonSupersequence
  25. Count distinct palindromic subsequences? → Interval DP, subtract the double countDPVariants#countPalindromicSubsequences

Trees & Range Structures

  1. Visit every node with a value flowing up? → One post-order returning a value (and a global for the answer)BinaryTree#diameter
  2. Answer per level? → BFS with a level-size snapshotBinaryTree#levelOrder
  3. Best path that may bend at a node? → Return best downward gain, update global with the bent pathBinaryTree#maxPathSum
  4. Count paths with a given sum? → Prefix-sum map along the root path, backtrackBinaryTree#pathSumIII
  5. Lowest common ancestor? → Post-order: both sides non-null means this nodeBinaryTree#lowestCommonAncestor
  6. Rebuild or store a tree? → Preorder + inorder map, or preorder with null markersBinaryTree#serialize
  7. Choose nodes with no two adjacent (tree dp)? → Return {take, skip} per nodeBinaryTree#robTree
  8. Validate or order-query a BST? → Carry bounds; use inorder = sortedBST#isValidBST
  9. Kth smallest in a BST, or lazy iteration? → Iterative inorder / stack of left spineBST#kthSmallest
  10. Prefix queries over many words? → TrieTrie#insert
  11. Find words on a board? → Trie + grid DFS with pruningTrie#findWords
  12. Maximum XOR of two numbers? → Binary trie, greedy opposite bitTrie#findMaximumXOR
  13. Many range sums, no updates? → Prefix sumsRangeStructures#prefix
  14. Point updates plus prefix sums, or counting inversions? → Fenwick treeRangeStructures#countInversions
  15. Range updates and range queries? → Lazy segment treeRangeStructures#LazySeg
  16. Count moves or flow along each edge? → Return subtree excess, add |excess|TreesVariants#distributeCoins
  17. Spread outward from a start node? → One DFS returning depth or negative distanceTreesVariants#amountOfTime
  18. Find repeated subtrees? → Canonical id per subtreeTreesVariants#findDuplicateSubtrees
  19. Enumerate all trees of a kind? → Choose root, combine left x rightTreesVariants#generateTrees
  20. Count nodes of a complete tree quickly? → Compare leftmost and rightmost depthTreesVariants#countNodes
  21. Rebuild from inorder + postorder? → Consume postorder from the end, right firstTreesVariants#buildTreeInPost
  22. Width of a level? → Heap indices, subtract the level's firstTreesVariants#widthOfBinaryTree

Arrays & Hashing

  1. Pair that hits a target? → Value to index mapArraysHashing#twoSum
  2. Count contiguous subarrays with a sum condition (negatives allowed)? → Prefix sum + frequency mapArraysHashing#subarraySum
  3. Longest subarray with equal 0s and 1s? → Map 0 to -1, first-seen index of each balanceArraysHashing#findMaxLength
  4. Product / aggregate of everything except self? → Left pass then right passArraysHashing#productExceptSelf
  5. Values in 1..n, find missing or duplicate? → Cyclic sort or Floyd on i to a[i]ArraysHashing#firstMissingPositive
  6. Majority element? → Boyer-Moore voteArraysHashing#majorityElement
  7. Sort three kinds in place? → Dutch national flagArraysHashing#sortColors
  8. Top K by frequency in O(n)? → Bucket by frequencyArraysHashing#topKFrequent
  9. Count pairs i < j with a value relation? → Merge sort counting (or Fenwick on ranks)ArraysVariants#countRangeSum
  10. Maximum subarray on a circular array? → max(linear best, total - linear worst)ArraysVariants#maxSubarraySumCircular
  11. Elements appearing more than n/k times? → Boyer-Moore with k - 1 candidates, then verifyArraysVariants#majorityElementII
  12. Most independent chunks to sort? → Cut where prefix max <= suffix minArraysVariants#maxChunksToSortedII
  13. Furthest pair with a[i] <= a[j]? → Decreasing stack of left candidates, sweep rightArraysVariants#maxWidthRamp
  14. Values in 1..n, find duplicates in O(1) space? → Negate a[|x| - 1] as a visited markArraysVariants#findDuplicates
  15. Sort integers in linear time? → Radix or counting sortArraysVariants#radixSort

Sliding Window & Two Pointers

  1. Longest substring / subarray satisfying a condition? → Variable window; update after shrinkingSlidingWindowPointers#lengthOfLongestSubstring
  2. Shortest window covering requirements? → Variable window; update inside the shrink loopSlidingWindowPointers#minWindow
  3. Count subarrays with exactly K distinct? → atMost(K) minus atMost(K - 1)SlidingWindowPointers#subarraysWithKDistinct
  4. Window of fixed size, anagram check? → Fixed window with a difference counterSlidingWindowPointers#findAnagrams
  5. Sorted array, pair or triple sums? → Sort + two pointersSlidingWindowPointers#threeSum
  6. Maximize area between two walls? → Move the shorter wallSlidingWindowPointers#maxArea
  7. Product / sum below a bound with positives? → Variable window with running product or sumSlidingWindowPointers#numSubarrayProductLessThanK
  8. Window must contain t as a subsequence? → Forward match then backward tightenWindowsVariants#minWindowSubsequence
  9. Every character in the window appears at least k times? → Fix distinct count 1..26, slideWindowsVariants#longestSubstringAtLeastK
  10. Take items from both ends? → Complement: slide a window in the middleWindowsVariants#maxScoreCards
  11. Exactly k odd numbers or distinct values? → atMost(k) - atMost(k - 1)WindowsVariants#numberOfSubarrays
  12. Values within t and indices within k? → TreeSet floor / ceiling over the windowWindowsVariants#containsNearbyAlmostDuplicate
  13. 4-sum or k-sum? → Recursive kSum down to two pointersWindowsVariants#fourSum

Monotonic Stack & Deque

  1. Nearest greater or smaller element for each index? → Monotonic stack of indicesMonotonicStructures#nextGreater
  2. Largest rectangle / contribution of each element as min or max? → Monotonic stack with left and right boundsMonotonicStructures#largestRectangleArea
  3. Max or min of every window of size k? → Monotonic dequeMonotonicStructures#maxSlidingWindow
  4. Shortest subarray with sum at least K and negatives present? → Deque over prefix sumsMonotonicStructures#shortestSubarray
  5. Evaluate an expression? → Stack with operator precedenceMonotonicStructures#calculate2
  6. Nested brackets or encodings? → Stack of partial resultsMonotonicStructures#decodeString
  7. Smallest number after removing K digits? → Greedy monotonic stackMonotonicStructures#removeKdigits
  8. Sum over all subarrays of min or max? → Per-element contribution with left and right boundariesStacksVariants#subArrayRanges
  9. Pattern a < c < b in order i < j < k? → Scan right to left with a stackStacksVariants#find132pattern
  10. Collisions processed in order? → Stack of survivorsStacksVariants#asteroidCollision
  11. Expression with parentheses and precedence? → Recursive descent with a stack of termsStacksVariants#calculate3
  12. Pop the most frequent, ties by recency? → Frequency buckets of stacksStacksVariants#FreqStack
  13. Queue built from stacks? → Two stacks, transfer only when emptyStacksVariants#MyQueue

Heaps & Top-K

  1. K largest / smallest / closest / most frequent? → Heap of size KHeapsTopK#findKthLargest
  2. Single Kth element, average O(n)? → Quickselect with random pivotHeapsTopK#quickselectKthLargest
  3. Median of a stream? → Two heaps (max-heap lower half, min-heap upper half)HeapsTopK#MedianFinder
  4. Merge K sorted sequences? → Heap of (value, list, index)HeapsTopK#mergeKSorted
  5. Fewest rooms / concurrent intervals? → Sort by start + min-heap of end timesHeapsTopK#minMeetingRooms
  6. Rearrange so equal items are not adjacent? → Max-heap by count, hold back the previous itemHeapsTopK#reorganizeString
  7. Repeatedly pick the best available option as capacity grows? → Sort by unlock key + max-heap of rewardsHeapsTopK#findMaximizedCapital
  8. Median of every sliding window? → Two ordered sets of indices (removal is required)HeapsVariants#medianSlidingWindowTwoSets
  9. Choose k workers, minimize cost when pay depends on a ratio? → Sort by wage/quality, keep a max-heap of qualitiesHeapsVariants#mincostToHireWorkers
  10. Need decrease-key (Dijkstra, Prim) in a heap? → Indexed min priority queueHeapsVariants#IndexedMinPQ
  11. Maximum number of tasks with deadlines? → Sort by deadline, max-heap of durations, evict the longestHeapsVariants#scheduleCourse
  12. 3D water level or flooding from the edges? → Min-heap on the boundary, expand from the lowest wallHeapsVariants#trapRainWater
  13. Smallest k pairs from two sorted arrays? → Seed (i, 0), push (i, j + 1) after each popHeapsVariants#kSmallestPairs

Intervals & Sweep Line

  1. Merge overlapping ranges? → Sort by start, extend the last outputIntervals#merge
  2. Insert into a sorted disjoint list? → Three phases: before, overlapping, afterIntervals#insert
  3. Remove fewest to make the rest disjoint, or fewest arrows? → Sort by END, greedy keepIntervals#eraseOverlapIntervals
  4. Maximum overlap at any instant? → Sweep line with +1 / -1 eventsIntervals#maxOverlap
  5. Capacity over a route or time? → Difference arrayIntervals#carPooling
  6. Online bookings that must not collide? → TreeMap floor / ceilingIntervals#MyCalendar
  7. Intersection of two interval lists? → Two pointers, advance the one that ends firstIntervals#intervalIntersection
  8. Smallest interval containing each query point? → Sort both, sweep queries, heap keyed by sizeIntervalsVariants#minInterval
  9. Attend the most events, one per day? → Sweep days, min-heap of end days, drop expiredIntervalsVariants#maxEvents
  10. Cover [0, T] with the fewest clips? → Greedy furthest reachIntervalsVariants#videoStitching
  11. Dynamic set of covered ranges? → TreeMap of disjoint intervalsIntervalsVariants#RangeModule
  12. Union area of rectangles? → Sweep line with coordinate compressionIntervalsVariants#rectangleArea
  13. Room assignment with counts per room? → Two heaps: free rooms by index, busy rooms by end timeIntervalsVariants#mostBooked

Binary Search

  1. First index meeting a monotone condition? → Lower-bound template: while (lo < hi), hi = mid on trueBinarySearch#lowerBound
  2. First and last position of a value? → lowerBound and upperBoundBinarySearch#searchRange
  3. Rotated sorted array? → Decide which half is sortedBinarySearch#searchRotated
  4. Minimize the maximum (or maximize the minimum) with a feasibility check? → Binary search on the answerBinarySearch#shipWithinDays
  5. Smallest rate finishing in time? → Binary search on the answerBinarySearch#minEatingSpeed
  6. Median or kth of two sorted arrays? → Partition the smaller arrayBinarySearch#findMedianSortedArrays
  7. Latest value at or before a timestamp? → Binary search the history listBinarySearch#TimeMap
  8. Real-valued answer? → Fixed iteration count, not an epsilon testBinarySearch#sqrt
  9. Maximize the minimum (or minimize the maximum)? → Binary search the answer with a greedy feasibility checkBinarySearchVariants#maxDistance
  10. k-th smallest of an implicit set such as pair distances? → Search the value, count <= mid with two pointersBinarySearchVariants#smallestDistancePair
  11. Answer is a real number? → Fixed iteration countBinarySearchVariants#minmaxGasDist
  12. Where does the missing count cross k? → Search on a[i] - (i + 1)BinarySearchVariants#findKthPositive
  13. Best rectangle with sum at most k? → Fix column pair, prefix sums with TreeSet.ceilingBinarySearchVariants#maxSumSubmatrix
  14. Peak then two monotone sides? → Find the peak, search both sidesBinarySearchVariants#searchMountain

Backtracking

  1. All subsets / combinations? → Start-index recursionBacktracking#subsets
  2. All orderings? → used[] arrayBacktracking#permute
  3. Inputs contain duplicates? → Sort + skip equal siblingsBacktracking#subsetsWithDup
  4. Reusable candidates summing to a target? → Recurse with the same indexBacktracking#combinationSum
  5. Generate valid strings? → Track counts, only add legal charactersBacktracking#generateParenthesis
  6. Place items under conflict constraints? → Occupancy sets / bitmasks for O(1) validityBacktracking#solveNQueens
  7. Find a path of letters in a grid? → Mark visited in place, restore on exitBacktracking#exist
  8. k-th permutation, not all of them? → Factorial number system, no searchBacktrackingVariants#getPermutation
  9. Fill buckets equally (square, k subsets)? → Sort descending, skip equal-load bucketsBacktrackingVariants#makesquare
  10. Minimum removals to make a string valid? → BFS by number of removalsBacktrackingVariants#removeInvalidParentheses
  11. Symmetry cuts the search? → Search one representative per orbit, multiplyBacktrackingVariants#numberOfPatterns
  12. Settle debts with the fewest transfers? → Net balances, backtrack on the first non-zeroBacktrackingVariants#minTransfers
  13. Every way to parenthesize an expression? → Split at each operator, memoizeBacktrackingVariants#diffWaysToCompute

Greedy

  1. Can you reach the end / minimum jumps? → Furthest-reach frontierGreedy#jump
  2. Circular route, find the start? → Restart after any negative prefixGreedy#canCompleteCircuit
  3. Neighbor-dependent minimum assignment? → Left pass and right passGreedy#candy
  4. Split into the most self-contained segments? → Extend to the last occurrenceGreedy#partitionLabels
  5. Custom ordering decides the answer? → Comparator from an exchange argumentGreedy#largestNumber
  6. Pair heaviest with lightest? → Sort + two pointersGreedy#numRescueBoats
  7. Need the best past option when stuck? → Heap of passed optionsGreedy#minRefuelStops
  8. Smallest lexicographic subsequence using each letter once? → Monotone stack with last occurrenceGreedyVariants#removeDuplicateLetters
  9. Assign people to two groups minimizing total cost? → Sort by cost differenceGreedyVariants#twoCitySchedCost
  10. Forward moves branch a lot, reverse moves are forced? → Work backwards from the targetGreedyVariants#brokenCalc
  11. Largest number from one swap? → Last-occurrence table, swap with the best later digitGreedyVariants#maximumSwap
  12. Order to beat opponent elements? → Sort and match greedilyGreedyVariants#advantageCount
  13. Merge two digit sequences into the maximum number? → Best subsequence per length, merge by suffix comparisonGreedyVariants#maxNumber

Linked Lists

  1. Reverse all, a segment, or in groups? → Iterative pointer flip; pull-to-front for rangesLinkedLists#reverse
  2. Middle, or nth from the end? → Slow / fast, or a gap of nLinkedLists#removeNthFromEnd
  3. Cycle present, and where does it start? → FloydLinkedLists#detectCycle
  4. Merge sorted lists? → Dummy head merge; divide and conquer for KLinkedLists#mergeKLists
  5. Sort a list in O(n log n), O(1) extra? → Merge sort with slow/fast splitLinkedLists#sortList
  6. Palindrome or reorder using the second half? → Find middle, reverse second halfLinkedLists#reorderList
  7. Clone with arbitrary pointers in O(1) space? → Interleave copies, set randoms, splitLinkedLists#copyRandomList
  8. Remove runs that sum to zero? → Prefix sums, jump to the last node with the same sumLinkedListsVariants#removeZeroSumSublists
  9. Add one to a number stored as a list? → Rightmost non-9 trickLinkedListsVariants#plusOne
  10. Kth node from the end? → Two pointers with a gap of kLinkedListsVariants#swapNodes
  11. Reverse groups conditionally? → Count the group first, then reverse in placeLinkedListsVariants#reverseEvenLengthGroups
  12. Child pointers / multilevel list? → Stack of saved next pointersLinkedListsVariants#flatten
  13. Insert into a sorted circular list? → Walk to the insertion or wrap pointLinkedListsVariants#insertCircular

String Algorithms

  1. Find a pattern in linear time? → KMP prefix functionStringAlgorithms#kmpSearch
  2. Does the string repeat a smaller unit? → n % (n - pi[n-1]) == 0StringAlgorithms#repeatedSubstringPattern
  3. All occurrences / prefix-match lengths? → Z-function on pattern#textStringAlgorithms#findAllZ
  4. Substring equality or duplicates at scale? → Rolling hashStringAlgorithms#rabinKarp
  5. Longest palindromic substring in O(n)? → ManacherStringAlgorithms#manacher
  6. Arithmetic on huge numbers as strings? → Digit arrays with carryStringAlgorithms#multiply
  7. Parse with signs, spaces, overflow? → Single pass with long accumulator and clampingStringAlgorithms#myAtoi
  8. Count distinct substrings / longest repeated substring? → Suffix array + LCPStringsVariants#countDistinctSubstrings
  9. Many patterns in one scan? → Aho-Corasick automatonStringsVariants#AhoCorasick
  10. Longest prefix that is also a suffix? → KMP failure functionStringsVariants#longestHappyPrefix
  11. Canonical form under rotation? → Minimal rotationStringsVariants#leastRotation
  12. Pairs of words forming a palindrome? → Hash all words, split each word at every indexStringsVariants#palindromePairs
  13. Validate a number or format string? → Finite-state flagsStringsVariants#isNumber

Bits & Math

  1. Everything appears twice except one (or two)? → XOR fold; split by lowest set bit for two uniquesBitsMath#singleNumberIII
  2. Count set bits, powers of two? → n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bitBitsMath#hammingWeight
  3. Small set, enumerate subsets? → Bitmask loop 0 .. 2^n - 1BitsMath#subsetsMask
  4. Large exponent modulo m? → Fast exponentiationBitsMath#powMod
  5. Count primes up to n? → Sieve of EratosthenesBitsMath#countPrimes
  6. nCr modulo a prime, many queries? → Factorial and inverse-factorial tablesBitsMath#modInverse
  7. Repeating decimals? → Remainder to position mapBitsMath#fractionToDecimal
  8. Sum of bit differences over all pairs? → Per bit: ones x zerosBitsMathVariants#totalHammingDistance
  9. Linear recurrence for a huge n? → Matrix exponentiationBitsMathVariants#matPow
  10. Modular inverse with a non-prime modulus? → Extended EuclidBitsMathVariants#modInverseAny
  11. Factorize many numbers? → Smallest-prime-factor sieveBitsMathVariants#spfSieve
  12. Pick uniformly from a stream? → Reservoir samplingBitsMathVariants#Reservoir
  13. Weighted random pick? → Prefix sums + binary searchBitsMathVariants#WeightedPicker
  14. Josephus-style elimination? → f(n) = (f(n - 1) + k) mod nBitsMathVariants#findTheWinner

Data-Structure Design

  1. Evict least recently used? → Hash map + doubly linked listDesignStructures#LRUCache
  2. Evict least frequently used, ties by recency? → freq to LinkedHashSet buckets, track minFreqDesignStructures#LFUCache
  3. O(1) insert, delete and random element? → Array + index map with swap-deleteDesignStructures#RandomizedSet
  4. Merge per-user streams into a feed? → Heap over each user's newest tweetDesignStructures#Twitter
  5. Throttle requests per window? → Deque of timestamps or token bucketDesignStructures#RateLimiter
  6. Versioned reads by snapshot id? → Per-index history + binary searchDesignStructures#SnapshotArray
  7. Route keys to nodes with minimal remapping? → Consistent hashing ring (TreeMap)DesignStructures#ConsistentHash
  8. Implement a hash map from scratch? → Array of buckets, chaining, resize at load factorDesignVariants#MyHashMap
  9. Increment / decrement counters, read max and min in O(1)? → Doubly linked list of count bucketsDesignVariants#AllOne
  10. Ordered set without balancing? → Skip listDesignVariants#Skiplist
  11. Cache with per-key expiry? → Hash map plus expiry-ordered structureDesignVariants#TTLCache
  12. Membership in tiny memory, false positives acceptable? → Bloom filterDesignVariants#BloomFilter
  13. Type-ahead suggestions? → Trie with per-node ranked listDesignVariants#AutocompleteSystem

Level Calibration

Graphs

SDE2 bar: BFS/DFS variants, Dijkstra, Union-Find, Kruskal's/Prim's, topological sort, bipartite check — implement cleanly, discuss complexity, handle edge cases (disconnected components, self-loops, multi-edges).
SDE3 bar: everything above cold, plus recognizing which algorithm applies to a disguised/real-world framed problem, discussing tradeoffs (Johnson's vs Floyd-Warshall, Dinic's vs Edmonds-Karp), SCC condensation as a two-step technique, and reasoning about complexity on dense vs. sparse graphs without being told which.
Staff bar (for context): full flow/matching implementations, 2-SAT reductions, amortized analysis of DSU from first principles, choosing/justifying approximations for NP-hard graph coloring instances.

Dynamic Programming

SDE2 bar: climbing stairs, house robber, coin change, LIS, LCS, edit distance, unique paths, word break — define state and transition out loud, then code it, with the space optimization when asked.
SDE3 bar: knapsack variants and the loop-order rules, interval dp (burst balloons), bitmask dp, stock state machines, regex/wildcard matching, and converting memo to table without prompting.
Staff bar (for context): digit dp, dp + data structure optimizations (deque, binary search, segment tree), proving a greedy fails and DP is needed, and estimating state-space size to choose between memo and bottom-up.
Staff bar: explain the extra state and prove the transition is exhaustive; reconstruct the answer, not only its value.

Trees & Range Structures

SDE2 bar: all traversals recursive and iterative, level order, LCA, validate BST, kth smallest, build from traversals, serialize, trie insert/search.
SDE3 bar: max path sum, tree dp, BST delete, word search II, Fenwick tree for counting problems, segment tree for dynamic range queries, skyline.
Staff bar (for context): lazy propagation, persistent or offline-query tricks, choosing between Fenwick, segment tree and sparse table by update/query mix, Morris traversal for O(1) space.
Staff bar: pick between "return up" and "pass down" in one sentence, and handle the global-versus-return distinction cleanly.

Arrays & Hashing

SDE2 bar: two sum, group anagrams, product except self, longest consecutive, subarray sum equals k, merge sorted arrays.
SDE3 bar: first missing positive in O(1) space, next permutation, matrix rotations, trapping rain water, reservoir sampling and shuffle correctness.
Staff bar (for context): proving in-place algorithms correct, streaming variants (reservoir sampling, approximate counts), and choosing between sorting and hashing by memory limits.
Staff bar: recognize "count pairs with a relation" as merge-sort counting or Fenwick, and justify the chunk boundary rule.

Sliding Window & Two Pointers

SDE2 bar: longest substring without repeats, 3Sum, container with most water, minimum size subarray sum, move zeroes, merge sorted arrays.
SDE3 bar: minimum window substring, exactly-K distinct, character replacement, anagram windows, and explaining why the window logic fails with negatives.
Staff bar (for context): windows combined with deques (limit-bounded subarrays), streaming windows, and amortized analysis arguments.
Staff bar: the non-obvious window problems (subsequence window, at-least-k, concatenated words) and fluent atMost(k) subtraction.

Monotonic Stack & Deque

SDE2 bar: valid parentheses, min stack, daily temperatures, evaluate RPN, next greater element.
SDE3 bar: largest rectangle in histogram, maximal rectangle, sliding window maximum, basic calculator I/II, decode string, remove K digits.
Staff bar (for context): contribution-counting with stacks (sum of subarray minimums), deque + prefix sums with negatives, and amortized O(n) proofs.
Staff bar: derive the contribution formula (left span x right span x value) and handle ties without double counting.

Heaps & Top-K

SDE2 bar: kth largest, top K frequent, K closest points, merge K sorted lists, meeting rooms II.
SDE3 bar: find median from data stream, task scheduler, reorganize string, IPO-style greedy with heaps, smallest range covering K lists.
Staff bar (for context): sliding window median with lazy deletion, external-memory top K, and quickselect vs heap tradeoffs under streaming constraints.
Staff bar: sliding window median with removal, decrease-key via an indexed PQ, and ratio-sort-then-heap problems (hire workers, team performance).

Intervals & Sweep Line

SDE2 bar: merge intervals, insert interval, meeting rooms I/II, non-overlapping intervals.
SDE3 bar: sweep line with events, minimum arrows, interval intersections, employee free time, calendar problems with TreeMap.
Staff bar (for context): skyline with a heap or TreeMap multiset, interval trees for dynamic overlap queries, and offline processing of queries against intervals.
Staff bar: offline query processing, maintaining disjoint ranges in a TreeMap, and the sweep-line area problem.

Binary Search

SDE2 bar: classic search, first/last position, rotated array search, search insert, peak element.
SDE3 bar: search on the answer (Koko, shipping, split array), 2D matrix search, K closest elements, time-based map.
Staff bar (for context): median of two sorted arrays, binary search combined with other structures (rolling hash for longest duplicate substring), and arguing monotonicity precisely.
Staff bar: convert "min of max" and "max of min" into a monotone predicate and name the feasibility check before coding.

Backtracking

SDE2 bar: subsets, permutations, combination sum, generate parentheses, letter combinations, word search.
SDE3 bar: duplicate handling, palindrome partitioning, N-Queens, sudoku solver, restore IP addresses, expression add operators.
Staff bar (for context): pruning heuristics, bitmask-based constraint propagation, and recognizing when DP or meet-in-the-middle replaces brute force.
Staff bar: name the pruning rule (symmetry, bound, ordering) and show the effect on the search tree.

Greedy

SDE2 bar: jump game I/II, gas station, assign cookies, best time to buy and sell II, merge intervals.
SDE3 bar: candy, queue reconstruction, partition labels, largest number, task scheduler, valid parenthesis string, with a stated exchange argument.
Staff bar (for context): proving optimality or finding a counterexample fast, matroid-style greedy, and recognizing when greedy gives a good approximation but not an exact answer.
Staff bar: justify each greedy with an exchange argument out loud; digit-construction problems (maximum number, remove duplicate letters) are the common hard ones.

Linked Lists

SDE2 bar: reverse list, merge two lists, detect cycle, remove nth from end, middle of list, add two numbers.
SDE3 bar: reverse k-group, merge K lists, sort list, reorder list, copy list with random pointer, LRU cache from scratch.
Staff bar (for context): in-place operations with proof of pointer invariants, lock-free list intuition, and skip-list / unrolled list tradeoffs.
Staff bar: in-place, one pass, O(1) extra space; explain which invariant each pointer maintains.

String Algorithms

SDE2 bar: anagram checks, longest common prefix, reverse words, string compression, atoi, add/multiply strings.
SDE3 bar: KMP or rolling hash for substring search, repeated substring pattern, shortest palindrome, Z-function ideas.
Staff bar (for context): Manacher, suffix arrays or automata at a conceptual level, hash collision analysis, and streaming string matching.
Staff bar: know suffix array + LCP and Aho-Corasick well enough to write them, and be able to say why a trie of patterns alone is not enough.

Bits & Math

SDE2 bar: single number, number of 1 bits, power of two, counting bits, missing number, reverse integer with overflow checks.
SDE3 bar: single number II/III, sum without plus, range AND, bitmask subsets, fast power, sieve, fraction to decimal.
Staff bar (for context): modular arithmetic with inverses and nCr, bit tricks inside dp, and reasoning about overflow and precision systematically.
Staff bar: per-bit decomposition, matrix power, and correct uniform sampling are the recurring themes.

Data-Structure Design

SDE2 bar: LRU cache, min stack, insert/delete/getRandom O(1), implement a queue with stacks.
SDE3 bar: LFU cache, Twitter feed, max stack, time-based key-value store, rate limiter, snapshot array, iterator designs.
Staff bar (for context): thread-safety discussion for these structures, sharding and consistent hashing, and trade-offs between exact and approximate counters.
Staff bar: pick the structure, state each operation's complexity, and handle expiry, resize and concurrency questions as follow-ups.

CS — CHEAT SHEET

Cheat Sheet

Every signal, pattern and pitfall on one page. Print it, or save it as a PDF.

Graphs

SignalApproachTemplate
Unweighted, shortest path?BFS (multi-source if multiple starts; 0-1 BFS if weights are 0/1)Traversal#bfs
Weighted, non-negative, single source?DijkstraShortestPath#dijkstra
Weighted, negative edges possible, single source?Bellman-Ford (also detects negative cycles)ShortestPath#bellmanFord
All-pairs shortest path, dense graph?Floyd-WarshallShortestPath#floydWarshall
All-pairs shortest path, sparse graph?Johnson'sShortestPath#johnsons
DAG + need ordering/dependency resolution?Topological sort (Kahn's or DFS)TopoSortDAG#kahnsTopoSort
DAG + need longest/shortest/count paths?DP over topo orderTopoSortDAG#longestPathDAG
Undirected + dynamic connectivity/merge queries?DSUDSU#countComponents
Connect all nodes, minimize total edge weight?Kruskal's (sparse/edge-list) or Prim's (dense/adjacency-matrix)MST#kruskalsMST
Directed graph, need tightly-coupled clusters?Tarjan's/Kosaraju's (SCC), condense to DAG if there's a follow-upSCC_Bridges_2SAT#tarjanSCC
Need critical/fragile points in a network?Bridges & articulation pointsSCC_Bridges_2SAT#findBridgesAndArticulation
Need to traverse every edge exactly once?Hierholzer's (Eulerian path/circuit)EulerianPath#hierholzer
Boolean 2-variable clause satisfaction?2-SAT via implication graph + SCCSCC_Bridges_2SAT#solve2SAT
Assignment/matching with capacity constraints?Max flow (Edmonds-Karp/Dinic's) or bipartite matching (Hopcroft-Karp)NetworkFlow#edmondsKarp
Small N (≤20), must visit all nodes/subsets?Bitmask DP (Held-Karp style)BipartiteAndBitmaskDP#heldKarpTSP
Grid, board or string-transformation problem?Implicit graph: name the node, generate neighbors, BFS (bidirectional if both ends are known)ImplicitGraphs#wordLadder
Shortest path with an extra constraint (K stops, fuel, keys, obstacle budget)?Put the resource in the state: Dijkstra/BFS over (node, used), or Bellman-Ford capped at K+1 roundsDijkstraVariants#cheapestFlightsDijkstraState
Path cost is the worst edge, not the sum?Dijkstra with max() as the combiner (or sort edges + DSU)DijkstraVariants#minimumEffortPath
Count the shortest paths, or print one?Dijkstra with ways[] or prev[]DijkstraVariants#countShortestPaths
Directed cycle, safe nodes, or an order inferred from data (Alien Dictionary)?3-color DFS or Kahn's, after building the edges from the dataCycleAndCourseGraphs#alienOrder
Ratios or equivalences between named things (evaluate division)?Weighted DSU, or DFS multiplying along the pathDSUExtended#calcEquation
Tree question: LCA, distance, diameter, an answer for every root?Binary lifting, double BFS, or rerootingTreeGraphs#treeDiameter
Small bipartite matching to code live?Kuhn's; Hopcroft-Karp only for large inputsMatchingColoringFunctional#kuhnMatching
Every node has exactly one outgoing edge?Functional graph: Floyd's or a timestamp walkMatchingColoringFunctional#cycleStart
Small k-coloring, or "can this be split into k groups"?Backtracking coloring (k = 2 is the bipartite check)MatchingColoringFunctional#kColorable

PatternUse caseComplexity
1D recurrenceCount ways or min cost where step i reads a few earlier stepsO(n)
Take / skipHouse robber familyO(n)
KadaneBest subarray ending here (track max and min for products)O(n)
Stock state machineHolding / not holding, transactions used, cooldown, feeO(nk)
0/1Subset under a capacity, each item onceO(nW)
UnboundedItems reusable (coin change, perfect squares)O(nW)
BoundedSplit count into 1,2,4,... chunks then run 0/1O(nW log c)
Subset-sum reductionsPartition, target sum, last stone IIO(n * sum)
LISLongest chain, each element larger than the previousO(n log n)
LCS / edit distanceTwo strings, match or edit prefixesO(nm)
PalindromesInterval dp or expand around a centerO(n^2)
MatchingWildcard, regex, interleave, distinct subsequencesO(nm)
Grid pathsRight/down moves, count or min/max path sumO(mn)
Max squareMin of three neighbors plus oneO(mn)
IntervalMatrix chain, burst balloons, cut stick, strange printerO(n^3)
Game dpScore difference the mover can forceO(n^2)
AssignmentEach worker takes one task, position = popcount(mask)O(2^n n)
Subset partitionFill buckets, track sum mod targetO(2^n n)
Game on a setMemoize on the set of numbers takenO(2^n n)
Digit dpCount x in [0, N] with a propertyO(digits * states)
dp + binary searchWeighted job scheduling: best profit up to the last compatible jobO(n log n)
dp + dequeWindow max over earlier dp valuesO(n)
Probability dpDistribution over states after k stepsO(k * states)
Memo DFSLongest increasing path in a gridO(mn)
Interval + extra stateRemove boxes, merge stones, palindromic subsequencesO(n^3)
Two walkersCherry pickupO(n^3)
Difference as stateEqual towersO(n x sum)
Flip the questionEgg drop: floors per move countO(k log n)
ReconstructionSupersequence, divisible subsetO(nm)
  • Max product needs both max AND min: a negative flips them.
  • Decode ways: a leading zero kills the one-digit option; 10 and 20 are the only valid two-digit zeros.
  • Stock with k transactions: if k >= n/2 it degenerates to unlimited.
  • Iterating capacity upward in a 0/1 problem silently reuses items.
  • Coin Change II (combinations) vs Combination Sum IV (sequences) differ only in loop order.
  • Target Sum: the reduction is subsets summing to (total + target) / 2; check parity and range first.
  • Russian Doll: sort width ascending and height DESCENDING so equal widths cannot chain.
  • Subsequence means order kept, substring means contiguous: contiguous resets to 0 on mismatch.
  • Regex star: zero copies is dp[i][j-2]; one more copy needs the preceding char to match.
  • Dungeon must run backward: the minimum health needed depends on what comes AFTER.
  • Burst balloons: think "last to burst" so the two sides become independent.
  • Pad the array with sentinels (1 at both ends) instead of special-casing borders.
  • Digit dp: tight is only true while every prefix digit equals the bound; started handles leading zeros.
  • Subset enumeration sub = (sub - 1) & mask totals 3^n across all masks.
  • Use Integer.bitCount(mask) as the implicit "how many placed" index.
  • When transitions look at a sliding window of earlier dp values, reach for a monotonic deque before a segment tree.
  • Longest increasing path needs no visited set: strictly increasing values make the graph a DAG.
  • State the dimension you added and what it stands for before writing the recurrence.
  • Interval DP with an extra state: memoize with the extra dimension, not just (l, r).
  • Reconstruction: keep a parent pointer or walk the table backwards, never recompute.

Trees & Range Structures

SignalApproachTemplate

  • Max path sum: return the best DOWNWARD gain (a path cannot fork upward), but update the answer with the bent path through the node.
  • Path Sum III: backtrack the prefix-sum map after both children return.
  • Recursion depth can hit 10^5 on a skewed tree; mention the iterative form.
  • Comparing a node only against its parent accepts invalid trees; carry bounds.
  • Recover BST: the first inversion marks first = prev, the last marks second = cur.
  • TreeMap gives floor/ceiling/first/last in O(log n) when a whole ordered structure is needed.
  • Word Search II: null out the stored word after finding it so duplicates are not reported.
  • Binary trie over 31 bits (not 32) for non-negative ints keeps the sign bit out of the way.
  • Fenwick is 1-indexed internally; the template exposes a 0-indexed API.
  • Count-smaller problems: compress values to ranks first, then scan right to left.
  • Skyline: process starts before ends at equal x and keep a TreeMap multiset of heights.
  • Width with heap indices overflows: subtract the level's first index.
  • Building from postorder: take the root from the end and build the RIGHT subtree first.
  • Shared subtrees in enumeration are fine if the trees are only read afterwards.

  • Negative mod: normalize with ((x % k) + k) % k.

  • Circular max subarray: if all values are negative the answer is the linear max, not total - min.
  • Count pairs during merge, before merging, while both halves are still sorted.

  • Heap of size K for K largest is a MIN-heap; people reach for a max-heap by reflex.
  • PriorityQueue has no decrease-key: push duplicates and skip stale entries on pop.
  • Comparator subtraction can overflow; use Integer.compare for large values.
  • A PriorityQueue cannot remove from the middle in O(log n); use TreeSet of (value, index) pairs when a window slides.
  • Ratio problems: sort by the ratio first, then the heap holds the quantity you want to drop.
  • Duplicate values in a TreeSet collapse; key by index, or by (value, index).

  • Touching intervals: decide up front whether [1,2] and [2,3] overlap.
  • Insert interval needs no sort when the input is already sorted: three phases in one pass.

  • Compute mid as lo + (hi - lo) / 2 to avoid overflow.
  • Search-on-answer needs a monotone predicate: if feasible(x) does not imply feasible(x + 1) you cannot binary search.
  • With duplicates in a rotated array, equal ends force a linear shrink (worst case O(n)).
  • Maximize-the-minimum searches the last true: use mid = lo + (hi - lo + 1) / 2.
  • Real-valued search: iterate a fixed count instead of testing hi - lo > eps.
  • Check the feasibility function is monotone before building on it.

  • Add a COPY of the current path to the result, not the live list.
  • Duplicates: i > start && a[i] == a[i-1] for combinations; used[i-1] check for permutations.
  • Prune before recursing (remaining sum < 0, not enough elements left) instead of after.
  • Equal-state siblings explore the same subtree: skip a bucket with the same load as an earlier one.
  • Undo exactly what you did (restore cells, pop path entries, reset lengths).
  • If the question asks for the k-th item, do not enumerate.

  • Largest Number: compare a+b with b+a, and special-case an all-zero result.

  • Work-backwards problems: divide or subtract from the target instead of multiplying from the start.
  • Sort stability and ties matter when the derived key can be equal.

  • KMP failure function: on mismatch fall back with k = pi[k - 1], never reset to 0.
  • Rabin-Karp: single mod hashes collide on adversarial inputs; use two moduli and verify with startsWith.
  • atoi: clamp as you accumulate, using long, before overflow.
  • Suffix array: sort by doubling ranks, then Kasai builds LCP in O(n).
  • Aho-Corasick needs fail links built by BFS, and output links to report all matches.
  • Parsing problems: write the state machine on paper first; flags beat regex.

Traversal Primitives

The base every other pattern builds on. If weights are capped or small, the interview signal is recognizing you don't need Dijkstra by default.

// … imports hidden
import java.util.*;

public class Traversal {

    // ---------- DFS (iterative, avoids stack overflow on deep graphs) ----------
    static void dfs(int start, List<List<Integer>> adj) {
        boolean[] visited = new boolean[adj.size()];
        Deque<Integer> stack = new ArrayDeque<>();
        stack.push(start);
        while (!stack.isEmpty()) {
            int u = stack.pop();
            if (visited[u]) continue;
            visited[u] = true;
            // process u here
            for (int v : adj.get(u)) if (!visited[v]) stack.push(v);
        }
    }

    // ---------- DFS (recursive) ----------
    static void dfsRec(int u, List<List<Integer>> adj, boolean[] visited) {
        visited[u] = true;
        // process u here
        for (int v : adj.get(u)) if (!visited[v]) dfsRec(v, adj, visited);
    }

    // ---------- BFS ----------
    static int[] bfs(int start, List<List<Integer>> adj) {
        int n = adj.size();
        int[] dist = new int[n];
        Arrays.fill(dist, -1);
        Queue<Integer> q = new ArrayDeque<>();
        dist[start] = 0;
        q.add(start);
        while (!q.isEmpty()) {
            int u = q.poll();
            for (int v : adj.get(u)) {
                if (dist[v] == -1) {
                    dist[v] = dist[u] + 1;
                    q.add(v);
                }
            }
        }
        return dist;
    }

    // ---------- Multi-source BFS ----------
    // e.g. rotting oranges / walls-and-gates: seed queue with all sources at dist 0
    static int[] multiSourceBFS(List<Integer> sources, List<List<Integer>> adj, int n) {
        int[] dist = new int[n];
        Arrays.fill(dist, -1);
        Queue<Integer> q = new ArrayDeque<>();
        for (int s : sources) {
            dist[s] = 0;
            q.add(s);
        }
        while (!q.isEmpty()) {
            int u = q.poll();
            for (int v : adj.get(u)) {
                if (dist[v] == -1) {
                    dist[v] = dist[u] + 1;
                    q.add(v);
                }
            }
        }
        return dist;
    }

    // ---------- 0-1 BFS (deque) ----------
    // edge weights only 0 or 1: push to front on weight-0 edge, back on weight-1 edge
    static int[] zeroOneBFS(int start, List<int[]>[] adj) { // adj[u] = list of {v, weight}
        int n = adj.length;
        int[] dist = new int[n];
        Arrays.fill(dist, Integer.MAX_VALUE);
        dist[start] = 0;
        Deque<Integer> deque = new ArrayDeque<>();
        deque.addFirst(start);
        while (!deque.isEmpty()) {
            int u = deque.pollFirst();
            for (int[] edge : adj[u]) {
                int v = edge[0], w = edge[1];
                if (dist[u] + w < dist[v]) {
                    dist[v] = dist[u] + w;
                    if (w == 0) deque.addFirst(v);
                    else deque.addLast(v);
                }
            }
        }
        return dist;
    }

    // ---------- Dial's Algorithm (bucket queue, small bounded integer weights) ----------
    static int[] dial(int start, List<int[]>[] adj, int maxWeight) { // adj[u] = {v, weight}
        int n = adj.length;
        int[] dist = new int[n];
        Arrays.fill(dist, Integer.MAX_VALUE);
        dist[start] = 0;
        // Circular buckets: every live tentative distance lies in [d, d + maxWeight],
        // so maxWeight + 1 buckets suffice. Memory is O(maxWeight), not O(V * maxWeight).
        int B = maxWeight + 1;
        List<List<Integer>> buckets = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < B; i++) buckets.add(new ArrayList<>());
        buckets.get(0).add(start);
        int remaining = 1; // entries still sitting in buckets (stale ones included)

        for (int d = 0; remaining > 0; d++) {
            List<Integer> bucket = buckets.get(d % B);
            for (int i = 0; i < bucket.size(); i++) { // index loop: 0-weight edges append to this bucket mid-scan
                int u = bucket.get(i);
                remaining--;
                if (dist[u] != d) continue; // stale entry
                for (int[] edge : adj[u]) {
                    int v = edge[0], w = edge[1];
                    if (dist[u] + w < dist[v]) {
                        dist[v] = dist[u] + w;
                        buckets.get(dist[v] % B).add(v);
                        remaining++;
                    }
                }
            }
            bucket.clear();
        }
        return dist;
    }
}

02 — SHORTESTPATH.JAVA

Shortest Path Algorithms

The follow-up interviewers ask: "your graph has 10^5 nodes but is sparse — why not Floyd-Warshall?" Johnson's is the answer that shows depth.

AlgorithmConstraintComplexity
DijkstraNon-negative weights onlyO((V+E) log V)
Bellman-FordHandles negative weights; detects negative cyclesO(V·E)
Floyd-WarshallAll-Pairs Shortest Path, dense graphsO(V³)
Johnson'sAPSP on sparse graphs, beats Floyd-Warshall when E << V²O(V² log V + VE)
A* SearchNeeds admissible heuristic; pathfinding/spatial/games~Dijkstra, faster in practice
ShortestPath.java
Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall, Johnson's, A*
varies
  • Weighted, non-negative, single source? → Dijkstra dijkstra
  • Weighted, negative edges possible, single source? → Bellman-Ford (also detects negative cycles) bellmanFord
  • All-pairs shortest path, dense graph? → Floyd-Warshall floydWarshall
  • All-pairs shortest path, sparse graph? → Johnson's johnsons
// … imports hidden
import java.util.*;

public class ShortestPath {

    // ---------- Dijkstra ----------
    // adj[u] = list of {v, weight}. Non-negative weights only.
    static int[] dijkstra(int start, List<int[]>[] adj) {
        int n = adj.length;
        int[] dist = new int[n];
        Arrays.fill(dist, Integer.MAX_VALUE);
        dist[start] = 0;
        PriorityQueue<int[]> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> a[1] - b[1]); // {node, dist}
        pq.add(new int[]{start, 0});
        while (!pq.isEmpty()) {
            int[] cur = pq.poll();
            int u = cur[0], d = cur[1];
            if (d > dist[u]) continue; // stale
            for (int[] edge : adj[u]) {
                int v = edge[0], w = edge[1];
                if (dist[u] + w < dist[v]) {
                    dist[v] = dist[u] + w;
                    pq.add(new int[]{v, dist[v]});
                }
            }
        }
        return dist;
    }

    // ---------- Bellman-Ford ----------
    // edges[i] = {u, v, weight}. Handles negative weights, detects negative cycles.
    static int[] bellmanFord(int n, int start, int[][] edges) {
        int[] dist = new int[n];
        Arrays.fill(dist, Integer.MAX_VALUE);
        dist[start] = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < n - 1; i++) {
            for (int[] e : edges) {
                int u = e[0], v = e[1], w = e[2];
                if (dist[u] != Integer.MAX_VALUE && dist[u] + w < dist[v]) {
                    dist[v] = dist[u] + w;
                }
            }
        }
        // Vth pass: if any edge still relaxes, there's a negative cycle
        for (int[] e : edges) {
            int u = e[0], v = e[1], w = e[2];
            if (dist[u] != Integer.MAX_VALUE && dist[u] + w < dist[v]) {
                throw new IllegalStateException("Negative weight cycle detected");
            }
        }
        return dist;
    }

    // ---------- Floyd-Warshall (All-Pairs Shortest Path) ----------
    // dist[i][j] = direct edge weight or Integer.MAX_VALUE/INF if none; dist[i][i] = 0
    static int[][] floydWarshall(int[][] dist) {
        int n = dist.length;
        for (int k = 0; k < n; k++) {
            for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
                if (dist[i][k] == Integer.MAX_VALUE) continue;
                for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                    if (dist[k][j] == Integer.MAX_VALUE) continue;
                    if (dist[i][k] + dist[k][j] < dist[i][j]) {
                        dist[i][j] = dist[i][k] + dist[k][j];
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        // optional: check dist[i][i] < 0 for any i to detect negative cycle
        return dist;
    }

    // ---------- Johnson's Algorithm (APSP on sparse graphs) ----------
    // edges[i] = {u, v, weight}, adj built separately for Dijkstra phase
    static int[][] johnsons(int n, int[][] edges, List<int[]>[] adj) {
        // Step 1: add virtual node connected to all with 0-weight edges, run Bellman-Ford
        int[][] extendedEdges = new int[edges.length + n][3];
        System.arraycopy(edges, 0, extendedEdges, 0, edges.length);
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) extendedEdges[edges.length + i] = new int[]{n, i, 0};
        int[] h = bellmanFord(n + 1, n, extendedEdges); // h[i] = reweighting potential

        // Step 2: reweight all edges: w'(u,v) = w(u,v) + h[u] - h[v]  (guaranteed >= 0)
        List<int[]>[] reweighted = new List[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) reweighted[i] = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int u = 0; u < n; u++) {
            for (int[] edge : adj[u]) {
                int v = edge[0], w = edge[1];
                reweighted[u].add(new int[]{v, w + h[u] - h[v]});
            }
        }

        // Step 3: run Dijkstra from every node on reweighted graph, then un-reweight
        int[][] result = new int[n][n];
        for (int src = 0; src < n; src++) {
            int[] d = dijkstra(src, reweighted);
            for (int v = 0; v < n; v++) {
                result[src][v] = (d[v] == Integer.MAX_VALUE) ? Integer.MAX_VALUE : d[v] - h[src] + h[v];
            }
        }
        return result;
    }

    // ---------- A* Search ----------
    // heuristic: admissible estimate of remaining distance to target (e.g. Manhattan/Euclidean)
    interface Heuristic { int estimate(int node); }

    static int aStar(int start, int target, List<int[]>[] adj, Heuristic h) {
        int n = adj.length;
        int[] gScore = new int[n];
        Arrays.fill(gScore, Integer.MAX_VALUE);
        gScore[start] = 0;
        PriorityQueue<int[]> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> a[1] - b[1]); // {node, fScore}
        pq.add(new int[]{start, h.estimate(start)});
        while (!pq.isEmpty()) {
            int[] cur = pq.poll();
            int u = cur[0];
            if (u == target) return gScore[u];
            for (int[] edge : adj[u]) {
                int v = edge[0], w = edge[1];
                int tentative = gScore[u] + w;
                if (tentative < gScore[v]) {
                    gScore[v] = tentative;
                    pq.add(new int[]{v, tentative + h.estimate(v)});
                }
            }
        }
        return -1; // unreachable
    }
}

03 — TOPOSORTDAG.JAVA

Topological Sort & DAG Patterns

Works only on Directed Acyclic Graphs. Once topologically sorted, many problems reduce to simple DP over the order — longest/shortest path, counting paths, critical path scheduling.

TechniqueIdea
Kahn's (BFS)Queue of zero-in-degree nodes; fewer than V processed at the end → cycle exists
DFS-based topo sortPost-order push onto a stack; reverse at the end
DAG DPRelax edges in topo order — no need for Dijkstra since a DAG has no cycles
TopoSortDAG.java
Kahn's, DFS-based topo sort, DAG longest-path &amp; path-counting DP
O(V+E)
  • DAG + need ordering/dependency resolution? → Topological sort (Kahn's or DFS) kahnsTopoSort
  • DAG + need longest/shortest/count paths? → DP over topo order longestPathDAG
// … imports hidden
import java.util.*;

public class TopoSortDAG {

    // ---------- Kahn's Algorithm (BFS, in-degree based) ----------
    // Also detects cycles: if result.size() < n, graph has a cycle
    static List<Integer> kahnsTopoSort(int n, List<List<Integer>> adj) {
        int[] inDegree = new int[n];
        for (List<Integer> neighbors : adj) {
            for (int v : neighbors) inDegree[v]++;
        }
        Queue<Integer> q = new ArrayDeque<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (inDegree[i] == 0) q.add(i);

        List<Integer> order = new ArrayList<>();
        while (!q.isEmpty()) {
            int u = q.poll();
            order.add(u);
            for (int v : adj.get(u)) {
                if (--inDegree[v] == 0) q.add(v);
            }
        }
        if (order.size() != n) throw new IllegalStateException("Cycle detected — not a DAG");
        return order;
    }

    // ---------- DFS-based Topo Sort ----------
    static List<Integer> dfsTopoSort(int n, List<List<Integer>> adj) {
        boolean[] visited = new boolean[n];
        boolean[] onStack = new boolean[n]; // for cycle detection
        Deque<Integer> stack = new ArrayDeque<>();

        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            if (!visited[i]) dfs(i, adj, visited, onStack, stack);
        }
        List<Integer> order = new ArrayList<>();
        while (!stack.isEmpty()) order.add(stack.pop());
        return order;
    }

    // … dfs(): helper hidden
    private static void dfs(int u, List<List<Integer>> adj, boolean[] visited, boolean[] onStack, Deque<Integer> stack) {
        visited[u] = true;
        onStack[u] = true;
        for (int v : adj.get(u)) {
            if (onStack[v]) throw new IllegalStateException("Cycle detected — not a DAG");
            if (!visited[v]) dfs(v, adj, visited, onStack, stack);
        }
        onStack[u] = false;
        stack.push(u);
    }

    // ---------- DAG DP: Longest Path (relax edges in topo order, no Dijkstra needed) ----------
    // adjW[u] = list of {v, weight}. O(V+E), no V x V matrix.
    static int[] longestPathDAG(int n, List<int[]>[] adjW, int start) {
        List<List<Integer>> adj = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int u = 0; u < n; u++) {
            List<Integer> nbrs = new ArrayList<>();
            for (int[] e : adjW[u]) nbrs.add(e[0]);
            adj.add(nbrs);
        }
        List<Integer> topo = kahnsTopoSort(n, adj); // throws if the graph has a cycle
        int[] dist = new int[n];
        Arrays.fill(dist, Integer.MIN_VALUE);
        dist[start] = 0;
        for (int u : topo) {
            if (dist[u] == Integer.MIN_VALUE) continue; // unreachable from start
            for (int[] e : adjW[u]) {
                dist[e[0]] = Math.max(dist[e[0]], dist[u] + e[1]);
            }
        }
        return dist;
    }

    // ---------- DAG DP: Count Paths from source to each node ----------
    static long[] countPathsDAG(int n, List<List<Integer>> adj, int start) {
        List<Integer> topo = kahnsTopoSort(n, adj);
        long[] ways = new long[n];
        ways[start] = 1;
        for (int u : topo) {
            if (ways[u] == 0) continue;
            for (int v : adj.get(u)) ways[v] += ways[u];
        }
        return ways;
    }
}

04 — DSU.JAVA

Disjoint Set Union / Union-Find

Manages partitions rather than traversing edges directly. Any problem with "connect/merge" operations interleaved with "are X and Y connected?" queries is DSU, not per-query BFS/DFS.

OperationComplexity
find() with path compressionO(α(N)) amortized
union() by rank/sizeO(α(N)) amortized

Primary uses: cycle detection in undirected graphs, connected-components queries, Kruskal's MST, offline queries, accounts-merge/equivalence-class problems.

DSU.java
Union-Find with path compression + union by rank, plus cycle/component helpers
O(α(N))
  • Undirected + dynamic connectivity/merge queries? → DSU countComponents
public class DSU {
    int[] parent, rank_;
    int components;

    DSU(int n) {
        parent = new int[n];
        rank_ = new int[n];
        components = n;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) parent[i] = i;
    }

    int find(int x) {
        if (parent[x] != x) parent[x] = find(parent[x]); // path compression
        return parent[x];
    }

    // returns false if x and y were already connected (i.e. this union closes a cycle)
    boolean union(int x, int y) {
        int rx = find(x), ry = find(y);
        if (rx == ry) return false;
        if (rank_[rx] < rank_[ry]) { int tmp = rx; rx = ry; ry = tmp; }
        parent[ry] = rx;
        if (rank_[rx] == rank_[ry]) rank_[rx]++;
        components--;
        return true;
    }

    boolean connected(int x, int y) {
        return find(x) == find(y);
    }

    // ---------- Usage: cycle detection in undirected graph ----------
    static boolean hasCycle(int n, int[][] edges) {
        DSU dsu = new DSU(n);
        for (int[] e : edges) {
            if (!dsu.union(e[0], e[1])) return true; // already connected -> cycle
        }
        return false;
    }

    // ---------- Usage: count connected components ----------
    static int countComponents(int n, int[][] edges) {
        DSU dsu = new DSU(n);
        for (int[] e : edges) dsu.union(e[0], e[1]);
        return dsu.components;
    }
}

05 — MST.JAVA

Minimum Spanning Tree

For connected, weighted, undirected graphs. "Minimum cost to connect all points" style problems are MST on an implicit complete graph — recognizing the implicit graph is the actual skill being tested.

AlgorithmBest forComplexity
Kruskal'sSparse graphs / edge-list input (sort edges, add via DSU)O(E log E)
Prim'sDense graphs / adjacency-matrix input (grow tree via priority queue)O(E log V)
MST.java
Kruskal's (DSU-based) and Prim's (priority-queue based)
O(E log E)
  • Connect all nodes, minimize total edge weight? → Kruskal's (sparse/edge-list) or Prim's (dense/adjacency-matrix) kruskalsMST
// … imports hidden
import java.util.*;

public class MST {

    // ---------- Kruskal's Algorithm ----------
    // edges[i] = {u, v, weight}. Best for sparse graphs / edge-list input.
    static int kruskalsMST(int n, int[][] edges) {
        Arrays.sort(edges, (a, b) -> a[2] - b[2]); // sort by weight
        DSU dsu = new DSU(n);
        int totalWeight = 0, edgesUsed = 0;

        for (int[] e : edges) {
            int u = e[0], v = e[1], w = e[2];
            if (dsu.union(u, v)) {
                totalWeight += w;
                edgesUsed++;
                if (edgesUsed == n - 1) break;
            }
        }
        if (edgesUsed != n - 1) throw new IllegalStateException("Graph is not connected — no spanning tree");
        return totalWeight;
    }

    // ---------- Prim's Algorithm ----------
    // adj[u] = list of {v, weight}. Best for dense graphs / adjacency-list input.
    static int primsMST(int n, List<int[]>[] adj) {
        boolean[] inMST = new boolean[n];
        PriorityQueue<int[]> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> a[1] - b[1]); // {node, weight}
        pq.add(new int[]{0, 0}); // start from node 0
        int totalWeight = 0, nodesAdded = 0;

        while (!pq.isEmpty() && nodesAdded < n) {
            int[] cur = pq.poll();
            int u = cur[0], w = cur[1];
            if (inMST[u]) continue;
            inMST[u] = true;
            totalWeight += w;
            nodesAdded++;
            for (int[] edge : adj[u]) {
                int v = edge[0], vw = edge[1];
                if (!inMST[v]) pq.add(new int[]{v, vw});
            }
        }
        if (nodesAdded != n) throw new IllegalStateException("Graph is not connected — no spanning tree");
        return totalWeight;
    }

    // minimal DSU inline dependency (see 04_DSU.java for full version with cycle/component helpers)
    static class DSU {
        int[] parent, rank_;
        DSU(int n) {
            parent = new int[n];
            rank_ = new int[n];
            for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) parent[i] = i;
        }
        int find(int x) {
            if (parent[x] != x) parent[x] = find(parent[x]);
            return parent[x];
        }
        boolean union(int x, int y) {
            int rx = find(x), ry = find(y);
            if (rx == ry) return false;
            if (rank_[rx] < rank_[ry]) { int t = rx; rx = ry; ry = t; }
            parent[ry] = rx;
            if (rank_[rx] == rank_[ry]) rank_[rx]++;
            return true;
        }
    }
}

06 — SCC_BRIDGES_2SAT.JAVA

Strongly Connected Components, Bridges & 2-SAT

After Tarjan's/Kosaraju's, the usual follow-up is: collapse each SCC into a single node and build the condensation DAG — that's often the actual second half of the question.

Stack depth: the DFS in these templates is recursive, which is the form interviewers expect. On a chain around 105 deep it overflows Java's default stack, so the file includes a runWithBigStack helper that runs the call on a thread with a bigger one.

Algorithm / PatternSolvesKey concept
Tarjan'sSCCs, single-passDFS discovery time + low-link values
Kosaraju'sSCCs, two-passDFS + transpose graph + DFS in finish-time order
SCC condensationCollapse each SCC into one nodeProduces a DAG for further topo-sort/DP
Bridges & articulation pointsNetwork vulnerability / critical edgesSame DFS discovery/low-link backbone
2-SATBoolean constraint satisfaction (a OR b clauses)Implication graph + SCC; UNSAT iff a var and its negation share an SCC
SCC_Bridges_2SAT.java
Tarjan's, Kosaraju's, SCC condensation, bridges/articulation points, 2-SAT
O(V+E)
  • Directed graph, need tightly-coupled clusters? → Tarjan's/Kosaraju's (SCC), condense to DAG if there's a follow-up tarjanSCC
  • Need critical/fragile points in a network? → Bridges & articulation points findBridgesAndArticulation
  • Boolean 2-variable clause satisfaction? → 2-SAT via implication graph + SCC solve2SAT
// … imports hidden
import java.util.*;

public class SCC_Bridges_2SAT {

    // The DFS below is recursive, which is the form interviewers expect. On a chain ~10^5 deep it
    // overflows Java's default stack. Run the whole call on a thread with a bigger stack:
    //   runWithBigStack(() -> result = tarjanSCC(n, adj));
    static void runWithBigStack(Runnable r) throws InterruptedException {
        Thread t = new Thread(null, r, "big-stack", 512L * 1024 * 1024);
        t.start();
        t.join();
    }

    // ---------- Tarjan's Algorithm (SCC, single-pass) ----------
    static int[] disc, low;
    static boolean[] onStack;
    static Deque<Integer> stack;
    static int timer;
    static List<List<Integer>> sccs;

    static List<List<Integer>> tarjanSCC(int n, List<List<Integer>> adj) {
        disc = new int[n];
        low = new int[n];
        onStack = new boolean[n];
        Arrays.fill(disc, -1);
        stack = new ArrayDeque<>();
        sccs = new ArrayList<>();
        timer = 0;

        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (disc[i] == -1) tarjanDFS(i, adj);
        return sccs;
    }

    // … tarjanDFS(): helper hidden
    private static void tarjanDFS(int u, List<List<Integer>> adj) {
        disc[u] = low[u] = timer++;
        stack.push(u);
        onStack[u] = true;

        for (int v : adj.get(u)) {
            if (disc[v] == -1) {
                tarjanDFS(v, adj);
                low[u] = Math.min(low[u], low[v]);
            } else if (onStack[v]) {
                low[u] = Math.min(low[u], disc[v]);
            }
        }

        if (low[u] == disc[u]) { // u is root of an SCC
            List<Integer> component = new ArrayList<>();
            int v;
            do {
                v = stack.pop();
                onStack[v] = false;
                component.add(v);
            } while (v != u);
            sccs.add(component);
        }
    }

    // ---------- Kosaraju's Algorithm (SCC, two-pass) ----------
    static List<List<Integer>> kosarajuSCC(int n, List<List<Integer>> adj) {
        boolean[] visited = new boolean[n];
        Deque<Integer> finishOrder = new ArrayDeque<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (!visited[i]) fillOrder(i, adj, visited, finishOrder);

        List<List<Integer>> transpose = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) transpose.add(new ArrayList<>());
        for (int u = 0; u < n; u++) for (int v : adj.get(u)) transpose.get(v).add(u);

        Arrays.fill(visited, false);
        List<List<Integer>> result = new ArrayList<>();
        while (!finishOrder.isEmpty()) {
            int u = finishOrder.pop();
            if (!visited[u]) {
                List<Integer> component = new ArrayList<>();
                collectComponent(u, transpose, visited, component);
                result.add(component);
            }
        }
        return result;
    }

    // … fillOrder(): helper hidden
    private static void fillOrder(int u, List<List<Integer>> adj, boolean[] visited, Deque<Integer> finishOrder) {
        visited[u] = true;
        for (int v : adj.get(u)) if (!visited[v]) fillOrder(v, adj, visited, finishOrder);
        finishOrder.push(u);
    }

    // … collectComponent(): helper hidden
    private static void collectComponent(int u, List<List<Integer>> adj, boolean[] visited, List<Integer> component) {
        visited[u] = true;
        component.add(u);
        for (int v : adj.get(u)) if (!visited[v]) collectComponent(v, adj, visited, component);
    }

    // ---------- SCC Condensation: collapse each SCC into a single DAG node ----------
    static List<List<Integer>> condenseSCC(int n, List<List<Integer>> adj, List<List<Integer>> sccs) {
        int[] compId = new int[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < sccs.size(); i++) for (int node : sccs.get(i)) compId[node] = i;

        List<Set<Integer>> condensedSet = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < sccs.size(); i++) condensedSet.add(new HashSet<>());
        for (int u = 0; u < n; u++) {
            for (int v : adj.get(u)) {
                if (compId[u] != compId[v]) condensedSet.get(compId[u]).add(compId[v]);
            }
        }
        List<List<Integer>> condensed = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Set<Integer> s : condensedSet) condensed.add(new ArrayList<>(s));
        return condensed; // this is now a DAG — run topo sort / DP on it
    }

    // ---------- Bridges & Articulation Points (undirected graph) ----------
    static List<int[]> bridges;
    static Set<Integer> articulationPoints;

    static void findBridgesAndArticulation(int n, List<List<Integer>> adj) {
        disc = new int[n];
        low = new int[n];
        Arrays.fill(disc, -1);
        bridges = new ArrayList<>();
        articulationPoints = new HashSet<>();
        timer = 0;

        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (disc[i] == -1) bridgeDFS(i, -1, adj);
    }

    // … bridgeDFS(): helper hidden
    private static void bridgeDFS(int u, int parent, List<List<Integer>> adj) {
        disc[u] = low[u] = timer++;
        int children = 0;

        for (int v : adj.get(u)) {
            if (v == parent) continue;
            if (disc[v] == -1) {
                children++;
                bridgeDFS(v, u, adj);
                low[u] = Math.min(low[u], low[v]);

                if (low[v] > disc[u]) bridges.add(new int[]{u, v}); // bridge condition

                if (parent != -1 && low[v] >= disc[u]) articulationPoints.add(u);
                if (parent == -1 && children > 1) articulationPoints.add(u); // root special case
            } else {
                low[u] = Math.min(low[u], disc[v]);
            }
        }
    }

    // ---------- 2-SAT ----------
    // n variables; each clause is {a, negA, b, negB} meaning (lit(a) OR lit(b)), where neg = 1 means the literal is NOT var.
    // Build implication graph: for clause (a OR b): ¬a -> b, ¬b -> a
    static boolean solve2SAT(int numVars, List<int[]> clauses) {
        int n = 2 * numVars; // node 2i = var i true, node 2i+1 = var i false
        List<List<Integer>> adj = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) adj.add(new ArrayList<>());

        for (int[] clause : clauses) {
            int a = clause[0], negA = clause[1]; // a: variable index, negA: 1 if negated
            int b = clause[2], negB = clause[3];
            int nodeA = 2 * a + negA, notNodeA = 2 * a + (1 - negA);
            int nodeB = 2 * b + negB, notNodeB = 2 * b + (1 - negB);
            adj.get(notNodeA).add(nodeB); // ¬a -> b
            adj.get(notNodeB).add(nodeA); // ¬b -> a
        }

        List<List<Integer>> sccList = tarjanSCC(n, adj);
        int[] compId = new int[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < sccList.size(); i++) for (int node : sccList.get(i)) compId[node] = i;

        for (int i = 0; i < numVars; i++) {
            if (compId[2 * i] == compId[2 * i + 1]) return false; // var and ¬var in same SCC -> UNSAT
        }
        return true;
    }
}

07 — EULERIANPATH.JAVA

Eulerian Path / Circuit

Traverses every edge exactly once — versus Hamiltonian, which is every node and is NP-hard. Don't confuse them in an interview.

TechniqueIdea
Hierholzer'sPost-order DFS with edge removal; reconstruct path by reversing the recursion stack

Classic problem: Reconstruct Itinerary (LeetCode 332) — included below as a worked shape.

EulerianPath.java
Hierholzer's algorithm, plus the Reconstruct Itinerary (LC 332) shape
O(E)
  • Need to traverse every edge exactly once? → Hierholzer's (Eulerian path/circuit) hierholzer
// … imports hidden
import java.util.*;

public class EulerianPath {

    // ---------- Hierholzer's Algorithm ----------
    // Directed graph, adjacency as multiset (use Deque so edges can be removed as used).
    // Precondition for Eulerian circuit: every node has in-degree == out-degree, graph connected.
    // Precondition for Eulerian path: exactly one node has out-degree = in-degree+1 (start),
    //                                  exactly one has in-degree = out-degree+1 (end), rest balanced.
    static List<Integer> hierholzer(int n, Map<Integer, Deque<Integer>> adj, int start) {
        Deque<Integer> pathStack = new ArrayDeque<>();
        List<Integer> circuit = new ArrayList<>();
        pathStack.push(start);

        while (!pathStack.isEmpty()) {
            int u = pathStack.peek();
            Deque<Integer> neighbors = adj.get(u);
            if (neighbors != null && !neighbors.isEmpty()) {
                int v = neighbors.poll(); // consume edge u->v
                pathStack.push(v);
            } else {
                circuit.add(pathStack.pop()); // no more edges out of u, finalize it
            }
        }
        Collections.reverse(circuit);
        return circuit; // if size != totalEdges+1, graph didn't have a valid Eulerian path
    }

    // ---------- Example: Reconstruct Itinerary (LeetCode 332) shape ----------
    // tickets = [["JFK","SFO"], ["SFO","ATL"], ...] -> lexicographically smallest valid itinerary
    static List<String> findItinerary(List<List<String>> tickets) {
        Map<String, PriorityQueue<String>> graph = new HashMap<>();
        for (List<String> t : tickets) {
            graph.computeIfAbsent(t.get(0), k -> new PriorityQueue<>()).add(t.get(1));
        }
        List<String> route = new ArrayList<>();
        Deque<String> stack = new ArrayDeque<>();
        stack.push("JFK");

        while (!stack.isEmpty()) {
            String airport = stack.peek();
            PriorityQueue<String> destinations = graph.get(airport);
            if (destinations != null && !destinations.isEmpty()) {
                stack.push(destinations.poll());
            } else {
                route.add(stack.pop());
            }
        }
        Collections.reverse(route);
        return route;
    }
}
